title: dedicated: autoscaler burst controls + improved fleet utilization reporting
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Add finer-grained burst controls to the Dedicated Fleet autoscaler and surface new utilization metrics to the fleet utilization reporting pipeline. Motivation: Customers running bursty workloads (short, high-concurrency spikes) observed over-provisioning or long cold-start tails because the autoscaler only used a coarse rolling average and permissive token-bucket defaults. This caused either wasted reserved capacity or missed throughput guarantees during sudden spikes. This PR introduces: 1) a tunable token-bucket burst controller per-pool with conservative default rate/credit parameters and an override mechanism per-customer; 2) revised autoscaler decision logic that combines instantaneous request queue length, recent throughput, and bucket credits to decide burst instance allocation; 3) new utilization metrics (bucket_credits, burst_allocations, burst_rejections, queue_latency_p95) emitted from the fleet controller and ingested into the utilization-reporting pipeline; 4) a lightweight smoothing policy for throughput guarantees to avoid flip-flopping during noisy signals; 5) telemetry pipeline changes to tag burst events by pool and customer tier and backfill 7 days of synthetic data for dashboards. Backwards compat: defaults preserve current behavior for pools that don't opt-in to the new bucket configuration. See sections below for commits, changed files, test and review notes.
commit_summary: feat(autoscaler): add token-bucket burst controller and per-pool config
feat(metrics): emit burst_credits, burst_allocations, burst_rejections, queue_latency_p95
fix(autoscaler): use combined signal (queue + credits + throughput) to decide burst adds
test: add unit and integration tests for burst controller and utilization pipeline
docs: document new burst tuning knobs and example configs
review_comments: Rafael Ortiz: The token-bucket math looks reasonable but can we add a safety clamp to avoid negative refill intervals? Also add an explanation comment referencing the original design doc.
Maya Chen: Added clamp in burst_controller.rs and linked the design doc in a comment. Also added unit tests for the edge case where refill interval becomes very small.
Priya Desai: Tests look good. One request: prefer explicit metric tag 'pool_id' rather than embedding pool in metric name to simplify Grafana queries.
Maya Chen: Switched metrics to use pool_id tag for burst_* metrics. Updated pipeline ingestion mapping accordingly.
Connor Blake: Integration tests flaked in CI on first run (race on simulated clock). Please make the test use a deterministic clock or retry logic.
Maya Chen: Reworked tests to use the test clock harness and added a flake guard. Re-run CI and it passed.
release_notes: Improve Dedicated autoscaler burst behavior and add per-pool burst metrics for fleet utilization dashboards. Administrators can tune token-bucket parameters per pool to balance burst latency vs reserved capacity. Includes backfilled synthetic data for dashboards.
notes: Performance impact: Microbenchmarks show a 12-18% reduction in unnecessary instance warmups for bursty synthetic workloads, and a 7% improvement in 99th percentile queue latency for multi-tenant pools that opt in.
Operational: New config keys: burst.token_bucket.capacity, burst.token_bucket.refill_rate, burst.max_burst_nodes. Defaults keep previous behavior unless overridden.
Rollout plan: Config gated behind 'experimental.burst_controller' feature flag. Staged rollout to 10% of pools in prod for 48h before wider enablement.
Follow-ups: Add automatic suggestions in Redwood Optimize based on customer traffic patterns (ENG-5012).
